analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 4, 2026)
key_insights: Democrats won control of Congress and lead gubernatorial elections, which the desk calls a move from Blue Wave to Blue Tsunami. The desk reads the result as a clearing event.
Markets whipsawed. The Tech/AI complex sold off materially at first, then bounced in Asia and in NDX futures off the lows. KOSPI closed higher after recovering more than 4.5% into the close.
The recovery is attributed to Trump saying he is 'absolutely willing' to accept the midterm results and work with Democrats, plus a recent positioning and performance wash-out.

The midterms matter for AI and data-centre (DC) concerns. Of 303 GW of planned US data-centre IT demand, 170 GW sits in states holding gubernatorial and legislative elections, and only 34 GW is in states with no relevant 2026 election.

In Texas, Hinojosa defeated Governor Abbott, which raises risk for DC construction. Drew argues the read is more bearish than reality: a governor's executive order can be challenged as unconstitutional, and a law would need a Republican Texas legislature.

The Democratic win is expected to affect US foreign policy, with Iran and Russia/Ukraine in focus, yet oil is trading higher this morning. The key question is whether it lowers the risk of resumed combat operations in Iran.

The desk expects geopolitical improvement to benefit international equities more than US equities. Aggregate HF exposure to the EU fell to historically depressed levels in October and recovered modestly into month-end, with relative exposure versus the US near multi-year lows.
Politico lists five things Europe needs to monitor after the Democratic win. The key risk is whether Europe bears the brunt of Trump's frustration.

Memory makers' 3Q26 results leave a positive bias: EPS and margin beats against FX headwinds, pricing upside, successful HBM price negotiation and volume delivery. Company-specific disappointments were Samsung Electronics' lack of an imminent shareholder return and Kioxia's weak CY4Q26 guidance, both seen as temporary.

The desk expects Samsung's shareholder return catalyst to return in January 2027 and Kioxia's CY1Q27 growth to be above seasonal and ahead of peers. It believes memory supply and demand fundamentals stay very solid through 2028E.

China A-share strategy: CSI-300/500/1000 are down 22%/31%/31% from their June peaks, so the core question is whether the market is cheap enough to buy. Central-government-backed capital bought A-shares over the past two weeks, and the twin regulatory meetings on 2 Nov on capital market support signal a policy floor.

Investors are still waiting for a durable bottom confirmed by liquidity and earnings. The China team keeps a barbell of defensive high yielders and growth, and the pullback has made wafer fab equipment and backend equipment attractive alongside memory and server/switch ODM/OEM, trading near historical means on forward P/S.

Market Intelligence view: tactically bullish on global equities. The regional preference stays long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus the EU, because the US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation and Asia has pockets of both.

Broadening can return, more clearly in US than EU. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but the desk needs stability in EGB spreads before conviction in EU broadening rises.

Longs: Tech and supercycle themes across infrastructure, less-levered hyperscalers and AI-vulnerables (AI and application software), plus EU and Japan banks, EU industrials, Japan machinery, GE Infra, EU miners, EU pharma, UKX and selectively the consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerables ex-software, short-cycle data centre capex names, EU insurance, challenged industries (autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, medtech) and MDAX.

Positioning Intelligence: October was a month most HFs will want to forget. Losses trace mainly to AI/Tech, even though broad US and European indices were flat to up. The desk sees multiple signs of de-risking that could point to an improvement, but the lack of capitulation before today, Middle East escalation concerns after the midterms and lingering AI worries limit conviction.

Prior -3z events in the 20-day long-short performance spread saw positive forward 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases. De-grossing has been prevalent, especially in multi-strats, and momentum exposure is at more than 12-month lows. Risks include quant de-grossing and still-elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.

US positioning drifted lower but not sharply. HFs cut net leverage earlier in October and added slightly this week, retail stayed sidelined, ETF flows stayed positive and CTA positioning is only at the 44th percentile in US equities.

The D1 team's Split Congress Pair (JPMSC26P) has rallied to 2-year highs. HFs are more bullish on Split Congress longs via short covering, mainly in health care, and shorts in capital markets stocks also saw buying. US banks have a strong November seasonal record, Financials ETFs had the strongest inflows last week and HFs remain net long banks.

Social media sentiment fell to the 6th percentile alongside a TMT-versus-defensives spread also at the 6th percentile, similar to prior episodes where Tech-led weakness was followed by Tech-led rebounds.

HFs flipped to buying biotech and medtech after months of selling, with health care flows the strongest of any sector last month. HFs kept selling Utilities despite the rally, leaving them with the lowest net positioning of any major industry.

EU positioning hit a low in the 5th percentile and rebounded to the 14th, which the desk says suggests room for further gains. HFs remain long EU banks and bearish on autos, luxury goods and software. China/HK aggregate positioning is the most bearish of any region.

vol_and_positioning: Global HF net returns were down about 4% on a rolling 20-day basis as of last Friday. The MTD estimate was -2.6% through Oct 29, likely near -3.5% after Friday. The global long-short spread was -2.2% MTD, with declines in Asia (-1.5%), N. America (-1.9%) and EMEA (-2.4%).

Prior -3z events in the 20-day L-S performance spread saw positive forward 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases, averaging +1%. Momentum exposure is at more than 12-month lows after heavy de-grossing, especially in multi-strats.

US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile as of Oct 29 with a neutral 4-week change. Retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile, ETF flows are +1z and CTA positioning is at the 44th long-term percentile in US equities.

Social media sentiment and the TMT-versus-defensives spread are both at the 6th percentile, matching prior lows that preceded Tech-led rebounds (late Mar 2026, Mar/Apr 2025, early Aug/Sep 2024, late Apr 2024, end Dec 2022).
EU positioning hit the 5th percentile before rebounding to the 14th. China/HK aggregate positioning is the most bearish of any major region at the 5th percentile.
HFs are net long US and EU banks, buying biotech and medtech, and selling Utilities, which have the lowest net positioning of any major industry.
The Split Congress Pair (JPMSC26P) is at 2-year highs on short covering, mainly in health care, with buying also in capital markets shorts.

tension_points.bull_case: Drew argues the bearish read is overstated. A governor's executive order can be challenged if it violates the state constitution, so DC construction is less threatened than headlines suggest.
tension_points.bear_case: Hinojosa defeated Governor Abbott, which raises risks on DC construction in a state within the 170 GW of planned demand located in election states.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A law would need assistance from a Republican Texas legislature, so a legislative move against DC construction would break the benign read.

tension_points.bull_case: Many signs of de-risking, momentum at more than 12-month lows, -3z spread events followed by positive 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases, and sentiment lows that preceded prior Tech-led rebounds.
tension_points.bear_case: Lack of capitulation before today, concerns about Middle East escalation after the midterms and lingering AI concerns make it hard to have strong conviction.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Quant de-grossing and still-elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning are named as risks to the rebound.

tension_points.bull_case: Europe earnings fundamentals are good and positioning is giving a buy signal, with HF exposure to the EU at depressed levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Secular themes carry less weight within EU equities, and Europe may bear the brunt of Trump's frustration after the Democratic win.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The desk needs to see some stability in EGB spreads for broadening to gain conviction in EU.
